items.stem: In a diagnostic-support context, a model's SENSITIVITY refers to its ability to:

options.text: Correctly identify those who truly have the condition
options.rationale: Correct: sensitivity is the true-positive rate among those with the condition.

options.text: Correctly identify those who are truly free of the condition

options.rationale: That is a performance (speed) property, not sensitivity.

items.explanation: Correct: sensitivity is the true-positive rate among those with the condition.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements reflect responsible use of a diagnostic AI model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Its output should be treated as decision-support that a clinician confirms
options.rationale: Correct: diagnostic AI informs but does not replace clinician judgement.

options.text: Its performance should be checked for different patient subgroups
options.rationale: Correct: subgroup evaluation guards against hidden bias.

options.text: A high overall accuracy means it is safe to use alone
options.rationale: Overall accuracy can hide subgroup failures and does not authorise standalone use.

options.text: Clinician review can be skipped once AUC exceeds 0.9
options.rationale: No metric threshold removes the need for clinician confirmation.

options.text: The model can issue a final diagnosis directly to the patient
options.rationale: AI outputs are not a standalone diagnosis.

items.explanation: Correct: diagnostic AI informs but does not replace clinician judgement.

items.stem: A model performs well in the hospital where it was trained but poorly in a new hospital with different scanners. This is an example of:

options.rationale: Correct: changes in the input distribution between sites degrade performance.

options.text: Overfitting to the test set only
options.rationale: The issue is a change between deployment settings, i.e. distribution shift.
Poor performance at the new site is the opposite of generalisation.

options.text: A calibration that is guaranteed to transfer
options.rationale: Calibration does not automatically transfer across sites.

items.explanation: Correct: changes in the input distribution between sites degrade performance.
